integrations.token_model: Human authentication uses Google OpenID Connect. Google ID tokens are signed JWT identity assertions. OAuth access tokens are separate bearer credentials for calling authorized Google APIs and are not used as the canonical E-7 identity assertion.
integrations.verification: Signature validation using keys obtained through dynamic OIDC discovery/JWKS; issuer validation (https://accounts.google.com); audience validation (matched to approved OAuth 2.0 client ID(s) for the E-7 application/client configuration); expiration validation; nonce/replay protection where applicable; hosted-domain validation only where deployment policy restricts access to approved Google Workspace / Cloud Identity domains. JWKS URI is discovered dynamically via provider discovery metadata and is not hardcoded in domain/business logic.
integrations.deployment_boundary: Organization-managed Google Workspace / Cloud Identity domain. Exact production organization/domain identifiers remain deployment configuration and MUST NOT be hardcoded in business logic.
integrations.provider_neutrality: Provider-neutral architecture is strictly preserved. app/integrations/... adapter boundary is preserved. Zero Google-specific fields in canonical E-7 public entities (no google_user_id or google_tenant_id as canonical domain IDs). Google sub remains stable external subject mapped via provider-neutral external_identity_mapping (provider/issuer, external_subject sub, E-7 principal reference). users.idp_sub is not frozen as a physical schema field; email is not used as canonical identity identifier. hd != canonical E-7 tenant_id. Tenant scope requires E-7 approved organization/tenant mapping and authorization.
integrations.secret_boundary: Zero secrets, client secrets, access tokens, refresh tokens, private keys, or production tenant credentials documented or stored.
integrations.service_authentication_baseline: Initial machine/service authentication mechanism uses service API keys in accordance with frozen Phase-1 baseline (OIDC/JWT + service API key). Google Service Accounts / Workload Identity Federation are classified as OPTIONAL_FUTURE_PROVIDER_CAPABILITY and are not required for Phase 1 service auth.

integrations.sync_reliability_rule: Google Calendar change notifications are an optimization and change signal, not the sole source of synchronization correctness. Notifications do not contain event payloads and Google does not guarantee delivery of every notification. Provider adapter design combines: (1) push notifications to reduce polling latency, (2) incremental synchronization via nextSyncToken as primary delta-retrieval mechanism (with HTTP 410 invalid sync token triggering full re-sync), and (3) optional periodic reconciliation/recovery as an E-7 resilience mechanism. E-7 scheduling remains canonical for E-7-owned scheduling state. Google Calendar remains authoritative for its native external calendar state. Synchronization must preserve the frozen external-ID mapping boundary in calendar_links.
integrations.provider_neutrality: Provider-neutral architecture is strictly preserved. app/integrations/... adapter boundary is preserved. No Google-specific canonical entity IDs introduced (no google_calendar_id). Google Calendar identifiers remain secondary external mappings in calendar_links within app/integrations/ adapter boundary.
integrations.secret_boundary: Zero secrets, client secrets, access tokens, refresh tokens, private keys, or production credentials documented or stored.
integrations.calendar_authorization_topology: CALENDAR_AUTHORIZATION_TOPOLOGY = TO_BE_CONFIRMED_DURING_IMPLEMENTATION. Valid approaches: delegated per-user OAuth, admin-authorized service account with domain-wide delegation, or another least-privilege model. Domain-wide delegation is not mandatory. Least privilege + admin policy + approved OAuth scopes.
integrations.time_handling: UTC_SAFE_TIME_HANDLING: Canonical scheduling instants may be normalized to UTC internally; original provider timezone metadata is preserved when synchronization requires it; Google Calendar all-day event date semantics are preserved; timezone/DST conversions handled explicitly; all-day dates are never converted into arbitrary UTC instants.
integrations.idempotency_architecture: E-7 owns synchronization idempotency (operation identity, external event mappings, persisted sync state, version-aware updates). Google Calendar does not provide generic idempotency keys; no Google Calendar idempotency-key API is fabricated.
integrations.sync_token_lifecycle: Persist nextSyncToken after initial sync; use for incremental delta queries; persist new nextSyncToken. If Google returns HTTP 410 / invalid sync token, local sync cursor is invalidated and full re-sync is performed to obtain fresh nextSyncToken. Not described as security-token rotation.
integrations.push_notification_validation: HTTPS callback endpoint; track issued channel IDs and expected resource IDs; unpredictable X-Goog-Channel-Token verified against expected stored value; X-Goog-Resource-State treated as resource-state metadata, not as authentication; notifications are change signals (do not contain complete event data); retrieve state via API.

integrations.direction_detail: E-7 emits notification commands and domain events to E-8; E-8 owns downstream delivery.

authority.scope: Sole authority for evaluating business conditions and deciding WHEN an operational event warrants notification
Authoritative for notification delivery state and functions assigned to E-8 by the source contract, including channel dispatch (email, SMS, WhatsApp, in-app)
Authoritative for atomic persistence of outbound domain events and notification commands with operational state in PostgreSQL

architectural_invariants: E-7 is an operations and orchestration engine, NOT a notification delivery platform
E-7 must not integrate directly with SMS gateways, SMTP servers, push notification services, or WhatsApp BSPs
E-7 is authoritative for deciding WHEN an operational condition warrants a notification (approvals, SLA warnings, blockers, schedule changes)

E-8 owns downstream notification/engagement delivery behavior as defined by its contract, including multi-channel dispatch across email, SMS, WhatsApp, and in-app channels (Complete Specification Sec. 22)
E-7 emits notification commands and domain events via the E-7 transactional outbox persisted atomically with canonical state in PostgreSQL to guarantee consistency (ADR-005)
Notification commands must be idempotent using deterministic command/event IDs
